newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says ambivalent on ending ethanol subsidy.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says ambivalent on ending ethanol subsidy.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Tuesday said the Clinton administration was undecided on a proposal by House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer to eliminate the ethanol subsidy.

"I'm not sure what I think on that at this point," Rubin said on "Newshour" program on PBS. "(The subsidy) was originally designed for a particular purpose, and I think we could probably go either way on that," he added.
Archer, a Texas Republican, proposed ending the subsidy by 2000 as part of a tax-cut package announced on Monday.
The Clinton administration has made separate proposals, which make no mention of ending ethanol subsidy.
